findings_to_judge.finding: The Q2 FY27 consensus of $2.68 EPS / $297.8M revenue has been unchanged for 60 days - i.e. it was never re-based after Q1 printed $3.24 vs $1.82 (+78%) and $291.0M vs $249.4M (+16.7%) - and it implies revenue up only 2.3% sequentially and EPS down 17% sequentially in Argan's seasonally strongest construction quarter, while the same analysts' FY27 annual estimate ($1.28B revenue, $12.09 EPS, 5 analysts, as of 2026-08-26) requires ~$330M and ~$2.95 per quarter across Q2-Q4.

Short interest is 1.02M shares - 7.38% of float and 3.28 days to cover as of the 2026-09-02 data date - on only 14.02M shares outstanding, and days-to-cover is up 65% year over year; the position was built during a 33% 20-day drawdown that the only article addressing it attributes entirely to a sector reassessment with no Argan-specific news.

In a Q1 10-Q footnote, contract liabilities (customer billings and advances ahead of cost) rose to $565.8M at 2026-04-30 from $514.0M at 2026-01-31 while $222.6M of revenue was recognised out of that balance - implying roughly $274M of fresh customer cash advanced in a quarter that recognised $291M of revenue, against contract assets of only $36.9M.

Backlog has now declined for two straight quarters from its peak - RUPO of $3.0B at 2026-10-31 per the Q3 10-Q, $2.9B at 2026-01-31, $2.8B at 2026-04-30 - and Argan has press-released and 8-K'd zero new power EPC awards in the three months since the Q1 call, the only 8-K being an $8.3M teledata bolt-on (ValCor, 2026-08-04), against management's Q1 guidance of 'a handful of new projects over the next 10 to 18 months' and add-on backlog additions of only ~$125M in Q1; on ~$320-350M of Q2 revenue that makes a third consecutive sequential decline to roughly $2.6-2.7B the likely headline.

Two state-level restrictions on data-center grid interconnection landed after Argan last spoke to investors on 2026-06-04 - Abbott ordered PUCT/ERCOT to audit data centers before approving new connections and ERCOT paused its 'batch zero' review (2026-08-03), and Pennsylvania restricted data-center permitting (2026-08-18, on which Talen fell 11%) - but the Texas order explicitly exempts data centers with on-site power generation, which is precisely the dedicated behind-the-meter gas plant Gemma builds.

Director John R. Jeffrey Jr. sold 5,716 shares at an average $579.64 on 2026-07-31, cutting his direct holding to 2,533 shares - roughly a 69% reduction of direct ownership, executed within 4% of the 52-week high and 41% above the current $412 spot.
